title: Hávamál
translation: Henry Adams Bellows, The Poetic Edda (1923)
note: The verses are from Henry Adams Bellows' English translation of the Poetic Edda (1923), which is in the public domain. Stanza numbers follow that translation. The 'means' lines are written for children.

verses.verse:
Within the gates ere a man shall go,
(Full warily let him watch,)
Full long let him look about him;
For little he knows where a foe may lurk,
And sit in the seats within.
verses.means: When you go into a new place, stop and take a good look around first. It is wise to know who is there before you walk in.

verses.verse:
Fire he needs who with frozen knees
Has come from the cold without;
Food and clothes must the farer have,
The man from the mountains come.
verses.means: Someone who comes in from the cold needs a warm fire, food and dry clothes. When a traveler comes to your home, help them get warm and fed.

verses.verse:
Water and towels and welcoming speech
Should he find who comes to the feast;
If renown he would get, and again be greeted,
Wisely and well must he act.
verses.means: A guest should be given water, a towel and kind words of welcome. And a guest who wants to be welcomed again should behave well and wisely.

verses.verse:
Wits must he have who wanders wide,
But all is easy at home;
At the witless man the wise shall wink
When among such men he sits.
verses.means: When you travel far from home, you need your wits about you, because things are easier at home. Wise people notice when someone acts without thinking.
Don't brag about how clever you are. Quiet, wise guests rarely get into trouble, and good sense is the best friend you can have.

verses.verse:
The knowing guest who goes to the feast,
In silent attention sits;
With his ears he hears, with his eyes he watches,
Thus wary are wise men all.
verses.means: A wise guest sits quietly, listens with their ears and watches with their eyes. Paying attention is how wise people learn.

verses.verse:
Happy the one who wins for himself
Favor and praises fair;
Less safe by far is the wisdom found
That is hid in another’s heart.
verses.means: It is a happy thing to earn kind words by what you do. Your own good sense is safer to trust than ideas hidden in someone else's heart.

verses.verse:
Happy the man who has while he lives
Wisdom and praise as well,
For evil counsel a man full oft
Has from another’s heart.
verses.means: Be glad if you have both wisdom and a good name. Bad advice often comes from other people, so learn to think for yourself.

verses.verse:
A better burden may no man bear
For wanderings wide than wisdom;
It is better than wealth on unknown ways,
And in grief a refuge it gives.
verses.means: Wisdom is the best thing to carry on a long trip. It is worth more than money in a strange place, and it helps you when you are sad.

verses.verse:
The son of a king shall be silent and wise,
And bold in battle as well;
Bravely and gladly a man shall go,
Till the day of his death is come.
verses.means: A king's son should be quiet, wise and brave. Everyone should go through life with courage and a glad heart, all their days.

verses.verse:
The sluggard believes he shall live forever,
If the fight he faces not;
But age shall not grant him the gift of peace,
Though spears may spare his life.
verses.means: A lazy person thinks that running from hard things will keep them safe forever. But nobody can run away from growing older, so it is better to be brave.

verses.verse:
He alone is aware who has wandered wide,
And far abroad has fared,
How great a mind is guided by him
That wealth of wisdom has.
verses.means: People who have traveled far and seen a lot can tell how wise someone else is. Seeing the world helps you understand people.
Enjoy good things, but don't have too much. Say what you mean or stay quiet, and nobody will call you rude for going to bed in good time.

verses.verse:
The greedy man, if his mind be vague,
Will eat till sick he is;
The vulgar man, when among the wise,
To scorn by his belly is brought.
verses.means: A greedy person eats until they feel sick. Eating too much can make others laugh at you, so eat what you need and stop there.

verses.verse:
The herds know well when home they shall fare,
And then from the grass they go;
But the foolish man his belly’s measure
Shall never know aright.
verses.means: Even cows know when they have eaten enough and it is time to go home. A foolish person never learns how much is enough.

verses.verse:
A paltry man and poor of mind
At all things ever mocks;
For never he knows, what he ought to know,
That he is not free from faults.
verses.means: Someone with a small mind makes fun of everything. What they never learn is that they have faults too.

verses.verse:
The witless man is awake all night,
Thinking of many things;
Care-worn he is when the morning comes,
And his woe is just as it was.
verses.means: Someone who doesn't think clearly lies awake all night worrying. In the morning they are tired, and the problem is still the same.

verses.verse:
The foolish man for friends all those
Who laugh at him will hold;
When among the wise he marks it not
Though hatred of him they speak.
verses.means: A foolish person thinks everyone who laughs at them is a friend. They don't even notice when people are being unkind to them.

verses.verse:
The foolish man for friends all those
Who laugh at him will hold;
But the truth when he comes to the council he learns,
That few in his favor will speak.
verses.means: A foolish person thinks everyone who laughs at them is a friend. But when they need help, they find out that few will speak up for them.

verses.verse:
A witless man, when he meets with men,
Had best in silence abide;
For no one shall find that nothing he knows,
If his mouth is not open too much.
(But a man knows not, if nothing he knows,
When his mouth has been open too much.)
verses.means: If you don't know much about something, it is often best to stay quiet and listen. Nobody will notice what you don't know unless you talk too much.

verses.verse:
Wise shall he seem who well can question,
And also answer well;
Nought is concealed that men may say
Among the sons of men.
verses.means: Wise people know how to ask good questions and give good answers. Whatever people say gets passed around, so choose your words with care.

verses.verse:
Often he speaks who never is still
With words that win no faith;
The babbling tongue, if a bridle it find not,
Oft for itself sings ill.
verses.means: Someone who never stops talking says lots of things nobody believes. A tongue that never rests often gets its owner into trouble.

verses.verse:
In mockery no one a man shall hold,
Although he fare to the feast;
Wise seems one oft, if nought he is asked,
And safely he sits dry-skinned.
verses.means: Don't make fun of anyone, even at a party. A guest who sits quietly and isn't put on the spot stays safe and comfortable.

verses.verse:
Wise a guest holds it to take to his heels,
When mock of another he makes;
But little he knows who laughs at the feast,
Though he mocks in the midst of his foes.
verses.means: A guest who makes fun of someone may soon need to run! Laughing at people can turn them against you, even when you don't notice it.

verses.verse:
Friendly of mind are many men,
Till feasting they mock at their friends;
To mankind a bane must it ever be
When guests together strive.
verses.means: Lots of people are friendly until they start teasing their friends at a party. When guests quarrel, it is bad for everyone.

verses.verse:
Oft should one make an early meal,
Nor fasting come to the feast;
Else he sits and chews as if he would choke,
And little is able to ask.
verses.means: Have a little something to eat before a big meal. If you arrive very hungry, you will be too busy chewing to talk with anyone.

verses.verse:
Crooked and far is the road to a foe,
Though his house on the highway be;
But wide and straight is the way to a friend,
Though far away he fare.
verses.means: The road to someone who doesn't like you feels long and crooked, even if they live close by. The road to a friend feels wide and straight, even if they live far away.

verses.verse:
Forth shall one go, nor stay as a guest
In a single spot forever;
Love becomes loathing if long one sits
By the hearth in another’s home.
verses.means: A good guest knows when it is time to go home. Even the warmest welcome wears thin if you stay too long.

verses.verse:
Better a house, though a hut it be,
A man is master at home;
A pair of goats and a patched-up roof
Are better far than begging.
verses.means: A little home of your own is better than none, because at home you are in charge. Two goats and a patched roof are far better than having to beg.

verses.verse:
Better a house, though a hut it be,
A man is master at home;
His heart is bleeding who needs must beg
When food he fain would have.
verses.means: A little home of your own is a good thing to have. It hurts the heart to have to ask others for every meal.

verses.verse:
If wealth a man has won for himself,
Let him never suffer in need;
Oft he saves for a foe what he plans for a friend,
For much goes worse than we wish.
verses.means: If you have worked hard for what you have, don't go without the things you need. Things don't always turn out the way we plan.

verses.verse:
None so free with gifts or food have I found
That gladly he took not a gift,
Nor one who so widely scattered his wealth
That of recompense hatred he had.
verses.means: Even the most generous person is glad to get a gift. And nobody who gives a lot minds being given something back.

verses.verse:
Friends shall gladden each other with arms and garments,
As each for himself can see;
Gift-givers’ friendships are longest found,
If fair their fates may be.
verses.means: Friends make each other happy by giving each other useful things. Friends who give to each other stay friends the longest.

verses.verse:
To his friend a man a friend shall prove,
To him and the friend of his friend;
But never a man shall friendship make
With one of his foeman’s friends.
verses.means: Be a true friend to your friend, and to your friend's friends too. Stay loyal to the people who stand by you.

verses.verse:
If a friend thou hast whom thou fully wilt trust,
And good from him wouldst get,
Thy thoughts with his mingle, and gifts shalt thou make,
And fare to find him oft.
verses.means: When you have a friend you trust, share your thoughts with them, give them gifts and go to see them often.

verses.verse:
Young was I once, and wandered alone,
And nought of the road I knew;
Rich did I feel when a comrade I found,
For man is man’s delight.
verses.means: Once I was young and traveled alone, and I didn't know the way. I felt rich when I found a friend, because people bring each other joy.

verses.verse:
The lives of the brave and noble are best,
Sorrows they seldom feed;
But the coward fear of all things feels,
And not gladly the niggard gives.
verses.means: Brave, good-hearted people live the best lives and don't dwell on sorrow. Someone who is afraid of everything is never at ease, and a stingy person never likes to give.

verses.verse:
My garments once in a field I gave
To a pair of carven poles;
Heroes they seemed when clothes they had,
But the naked man is nought.
verses.means: Once I put my clothes on two carved wooden posts in a field, and they looked like heroes! How you dress and look after yourself changes how others see you.

verses.verse:
Hotter than fire between false friends
Does friendship five days burn;
When the sixth day comes the fire cools,
And ended is all the love.
verses.means: Friendship between people who aren't truly friends can burn hotter than fire for five days. On the sixth day the fire goes out, and that friendship is over.

verses.verse:
No great thing needs a man to give
Oft little will purchase praise;
With half a loaf and a half-filled cup
A friend full fast I made.
verses.means: You don't need to give big presents to make a friend. Sharing half a loaf of bread and a cup can be enough.

verses.verse:
A little sand has a little sea,
And small are the minds of men;
Though all men are not equal in wisdom,
Yet half-wise only are all.
verses.means: A small beach has only a little sea. Some people are wiser than others, but nobody knows everything.

verses.verse:
A measure of wisdom each man shall have,
But never too much let him know;
The fairest lives do those men live
Whose wisdom wide has grown.
verses.means: Everyone should have a good amount of wisdom, but nobody needs to know everything. The happiest lives belong to people who know a good many things.

verses.verse:
A measure of wisdom each man shall have,
But never too much let him know;
For the wise man’s heart is seldom happy,
If wisdom too great he has won.
verses.means: Be wise enough, but don't try to know everything. A heart that carries too much knowing is not often happy.

verses.verse:
A measure of wisdom each man shall have,
But never too much let him know;
Let no man the fate before him see,
For so is he freest from sorrow.
verses.means: Be wise enough, but you don't need to know everything. Not knowing what tomorrow brings lets you live without worrying about it.

verses.verse:
A brand from a brand is kindled and burned,
And fire from fire begotten;
And man by his speech is known to men,
And the stupid by their stillness.
verses.means: One flame lights another flame. In the same way, people get to know you by the way you talk with them.

verses.verse:
He must early go forth whose workers are few,
Himself his work to seek;
Much remains undone for the morning-sleeper,
For the swift is wealth half won.
verses.means: If you have a lot to do and not many helpers, get started early. A late sleeper leaves things undone, and starting quickly gets the job half done.

verses.verse:
Of seasoned shingles and strips of bark
For the thatch let one know his need,
And how much of wood he must have for a month,
Or in half a year he will use.
verses.means: Know how much wood and bark you will need for your roof and your fire. It is wise to plan ahead for the months to come.

verses.verse:
Washed and fed to the council fare,
But care not too much for thy clothes;
Let none be ashamed of his shoes and hose,
Less still of the steed he rides,
(Though poor be the horse he has.)
verses.means: Go to important places clean and with a full tummy, but don't worry too much about your clothes. Nobody should feel ashamed of their shoes, or of a horse that isn't fancy.

verses.verse:
When the eagle comes to the ancient sea,
He snaps and hangs his head;
So is a man in the midst of a throng,
Who few to speak for him finds.
verses.means: When an eagle reaches the sea, it hangs its head. A person feels the same way in a crowd when nobody there will speak up for them.

verses.verse:
The man who is prudent a measured use
Of the might he has will make;
He finds when among the brave he fares
That the boldest he may not be.
verses.means: A sensible person uses their strength with care. When they are among brave people, they find out they may not be the boldest one there.

verses.verse:
Fire for men is the fairest gift,
And power to see the sun;
Health as well, if a man may have it,
And a life not stained with sin.
verses.means: Fire and seeing the sun are the finest gifts. Good health is a gift too, and so is a life lived without doing wrong.

verses.verse:
All wretched is no man, though never so sick;
Some from their sons have joy,
Some win it from kinsmen, and some from their wealth,
And some from worthy works.
verses.means: Nobody is completely unhappy, even when they are sick. Some find joy in their children, some in their family, some in what they have, and some in good work.

verses.verse:
A son is better, though late he be born,
And his father to death have fared;
Memory-stones seldom stand by the road
Save when kinsman honors his kin.
verses.means: A son is a blessing, even one born after his father has died. Stones to remember people stand by the road because family members honor those who came before.

verses.verse:
He welcomes the night whose fare is enough.
(Short are the yards of a ship,)
Uneasy are autumn nights;
Full oft does the weather change in a week,
And more in a month’s time.
verses.means: Someone who has enough food is glad when night comes. Autumn nights can be uneasy, and the weather can change a lot in a week, so it is good to be ready.

verses.verse:
A man knows not, if nothing he knows,
That gold oft apes begets;
One man is wealthy and one is poor,
Yet scorn for him none should know.
verses.means: Gold can make people act silly. Some people are rich and some are poor, but nobody should be looked down on for being poor.

verses.verse:
Cattle die, and kinsmen die,
And so one dies one’s self;
But a noble name will never die,
If good renown one gets.
verses.means: Animals die, family members die, and one day each of us will too. But a good name, earned by how you live, never dies.

verses.verse:
Cattle die, and kinsmen die,
And so one dies one’s self;
One thing I know that never dies,
The fame of a dead man’s deeds.
verses.means: Everything that lives will one day die. But the good things a person did are remembered long after they are gone.

verses.verse:
For never thou mayst from an evil man
A good requital get;
But a good man oft the greatest love
Through words of praise will win thee.
verses.means: You will never get a good reward from a bad person. But a good person will often speak well of you and win you friends.

verses.verse:
Mingled is love when a man can speak
To another all his thought;
Nought is so bad as false to be,
No friend speaks only fair.
verses.means: Real friends can tell each other everything they think. Nothing is worse than being false, and a true friend tells you the truth, not only nice things.

verses.verse:
Oft scarcely he knows who sits in the house
What kind is the man who comes;
None so good is found that faults he has not,
Nor so wicked that nought he is worth.
verses.means: When someone new comes in, you can't tell right away what kind of person they are. Nobody is so good that they have no faults, and nobody is so bad that they are worth nothing.
